question: How does Delta Lake achieve atomic commits for a transaction?
options: By locking the entire cloud storage account
By writing data files then atomically adding a new JSON commit to the _delta_log
explanation: Delta first writes the new Parquet files, then atomically commits a new numbered JSON entry to the transaction log; the table version changes only when that commit succeeds.

question: What concurrency-control mechanism does Delta Lake use for writes?
explanation: Delta uses optimistic concurrency control: writers assume no conflict, and on commit Delta verifies no conflicting changes occurred, retrying or failing if they did.

question: What isolation guarantee do readers of a Delta table get during concurrent writes?
options: They may see half-written, corrupted data
They must wait until all writes stop
They see a consistent snapshot and never partial writes
explanation: Readers operate on a consistent snapshot defined by the transaction log at read time, so they never observe partial or in-progress writes (snapshot isolation).

question: When can two concurrent Delta writers conflict and cause one to fail?
options: When they modify the same files/partitions in incompatible ways
explanation: A ConcurrentModificationException can occur when two writers touch overlapping files/partitions; disjoint writes usually succeed, while conflicting ones cause one commit to be rejected.

question: Why are periodic checkpoints written in the Delta transaction log?
options: To consolidate log entries into Parquet so reading table state stays fast
explanation: Delta writes checkpoint Parquet files (by default every 10 commits) summarizing state, so readers don't need to replay every JSON commit, keeping metadata reads efficient.
